Week 4 Project Instructions - Draft Event Requests
Draft requests should remain distinguishable from requests already submitted for review.
Draft status is supported. A last-modified timestamp is not explicitly required as a US05 customer outcome.
The saved event request has status "Draft" and remains distinguishable from a submitted event request.

Has the draft visible only to themselves
Week 4 Project Instructions - User Authorisation and Authentication; Notion US02 and US06
Access depends on role and relationship to an event. US06 separately governs viewing and editing one's own drafts.
Creator-only visibility is more specific than the Release 1 wording and duplicates the access/edit boundary already assigned to US02 and US06.
Removed from US05 Acceptance Criteria. Enforce authorised access through US02 and test own-draft viewing/editing under US06.
Avoids claiming an unsupported US05 permission while preserving server-side authorisation as a separate requirement.
Cannot submit a draft until all mandatory fields are complete
Week 4 Project Instructions - Event Request Creation and Draft Event Requests; current section clarification
The documents require an incomplete draft to be saveable. They do not identify a complete binding mandatory-field list for submission in the evidence available here.
The criterion assumes a confirmed mandatory-field list and concerns submission validation, which belongs to US03/US04 rather than saving a draft.
Removed from US05. Submission blocking must be handled under US03/US04 only where exact mandatory requirements are evidenced.
Separates draft persistence from submission validation and prevents unsupported validation rules.
Does not lose entered data when the browser session ends unexpectedly
Week 1 Customer Briefing - Draft Event Requests; Week 4 Project Instructions - Draft Event Requests
Saved incomplete information must remain available so the request can be completed or reviewed later.
Unexpected browser-session wording implies recovery of unsaved data, autosave or crash recovery, none of which is explicitly required.
The saved draft retains the event information explicitly saved by the Event Organiser.
Requires persistence of saved data without inventing autosave or recovery of unsaved browser state.
User Story purpose: so that I can complete it later; Week 4: return to it later and continue editing it
Week 4 Project Instructions - Draft Event Requests; original Notion US06
Release 1 requires the combined draft workflow to support returning later and continuing editing.
Adding reopen/edit as another US05 AC would duplicate US06, whose title and AC already own reopening and editing a saved draft.
US05 persists the draft and saved values; US06 verifies listing, reopening, restoring and editing the saved draft.
Maintains end-to-end traceability while keeping Story responsibilities small and non-duplicative.
Can view a list of their own draft requests with last-modified dates

Event Organisers can save an incomplete event request before submission, return to it later, and continue editing it.
Last-modified dates are not required as a customer outcome.
The Event Organiser can access their saved draft requests to return to them later.
A list is the current UI implementation choice; timestamps are not an AC.
Can reopen a draft with all previously entered values restored
Week 4 Project Instructions (2).docx — Draft Event Requests
Event Organisers can save an incomplete event request before submission, return to it later, and continue editing it.
Previously entered could include unsaved data.
The Event Organiser can reopen a saved draft with all explicitly saved event information restored.
Can edit, re-save, or delete a draft
Week 4 Project Instructions (2).docx — Draft Event Requests
Event Organisers can save an incomplete event request before submission, return to it later, and continue editing it.
Deletion has no written basis. Re-save should retain the same request identity.
The Event Organiser can edit and re-save the same draft before submission; the updated information replaces its previously saved information.
Supports continued editing without creating a duplicate draft. Deletion is excluded.
Can submit the draft once it is complete and valid
Week 4 Project Instructions (2).docx — Event Request Creation / Draft Event Requests
Event Organisers can create and submit event requests. Draft editing occurs before submission.
Submission and any evidenced validation are owned by US04.
Submission remains covered by US04 rather than duplicated as a US06 acceptance criterion.
Avoids importing the unsupported mandatory-field assumptions from the current submission code.
Cannot view or edit drafts created by another user
Week 4 Project Instructions (2).docx — User Authorisation and Authentication
Users should only be able to view or modify information appropriate to their role and relationship to an event.
No contradiction for the organiser own-draft workflow.
The Event Organiser can access and edit only their own drafts.
Server uses authenticated organiser identity and limits operations to Draft status.
